title: Provisioning cryptography and authority threats
summary: Cryptographic authorisation includes peer session identity, message provenance, quorum of delegated controller keys, monotonic epoch/revision/sequence, expiry/revocation and immutable trust roots. A signed packet alone is insufficient.
invariants: Source IP, MAC, ROUTE/XROUTE, XTP KEY and service string are not identity proof
Inbound remote requests bind an authenticated principal to established session and to owner delegation
Controller keys are distinct from node announcement keys; repeated signatures from same controller count once
Quorum signatures do not create a consensus log; distinct durable committed revision evidence is required
Two controllers use 2-of-2 writes; three controllers prefer 2-of-3 with independently fenced commit state
Never use a single writable mirror as a second independent vote
Raw private signing material must not be in LDAP attributes, route files, JSON examples, logs or Git
Canonical signed bytes reject duplicate JSON keys, floats, unexpected extensions, schema downgrade and size overflow
Revocation and epoch floors survive rollback and reinstallation or re-establish from trusted authority
procedure: Verify private key role, controller membership and trusted public key prior to record acceptance
Bind request to target MI/realm/nonce/policy digest/epoch/revision and expiry
Require authenticated encrypted XTP session (or independently qualified secure channel correctly bound to it)
Reject forged service owners, caller class promotion, route collisions, stale updates and duplicate signers
Stage only committed quorum-certified allocation; refuse mutable bootstrap trust

provenance.claim: 19 offline positive and negative contract tests

qualification_boundaries.native_security: gateway mutual remote KEY-bound authentication not qualified; effectful provisioning forbidden
